acceptanceCriteria: TSA-V0 requirements for a one-shot-ui-state-assertion rule (direct reads and reads through a resolved page-object method) and an advisory exact-text cross-variant rule, each with suppression semantics and a fixture that triggers it and one that does not (web-first toBeVisible/toHaveCount, expect.poll)
An unresolved helper body yields an UNKNOWN finding rather than silence; the depth of helper-following is bounded and stated
A cross-variant split at the same revision (playwright runs compare or a run receipt) names the exact-text locator as a likely cause; with no multi-project evidence the rule reports NOT_PRODUCED
Focused tests pass, and the build log records the limits and that no live qualification was run
body: GitHub issue #1114. Browser tests assert a single non-retrying read of UI state, for example expect(await locator.isVisible()).toBe(true) or expect(await locator.count()).toBe(3). The read happens once, so a slower renderer, loaded environment or cold cache fails the test even though the state appears a moment later. Web-first matchers (toBeVisible, toHaveCount) would wait for it. Observed: one test passed on one front-end implementation of a screen and failed on another. The cause was a one-shot isVisible() read hidden in a page-object helper and asserted with toBe(true). Test validity reported nothing, and diagnosis needed a trace. Related case: getByText(name, {exact:true}) can never match when one implementation renders extra inline content in the element, such as a badge span. Requested: (1) an advisory lint rule for expect(await X) where X is a UI-state read (isVisible/isHidden/isEnabled/isChecked/isEditable/count/textContent/innerText/inputValue), directly or through a page-object method whose body returns one. Following the method body is the useful part. (2) Best effort: when one test's pass/fail splits by project or variant at the same revision, report it and name any exact-text locator it uses as a likely cause. Both are advisory, can be suppressed with corvint-lint-allow plus a reason, and appear in the run receipt next to the failure they explain. Natural home: internal/testsource/lint.go (TSA-V0, rules no-assertion..skip-only-without-reason, delivered by V1-1589). A page-object method that can't be resolved must be reported as UNKNOWN, never as clean.
title: tests lint: one-shot UI-state assertions through page-object helpers, and exact-text locators behind cross-variant pass/fail splits (#1114)
